automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Automation scripts must execute steps in the exact order defined in test case steps: (1) Implicit Required Steps, (2) Supporting Steps, (3) Validation Steps. This order ensures proper application state progression.

automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Violation of step order will result in script rejection during code review
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Structure automation scripts with clearly demarcated sections: setup phase (implicit required), trigger phase (supporting), and validation phase (assertions). Use comments or method names to indicate phase boundaries.

automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all validation and verification test steps
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - All verification steps must have corresponding assertion statements
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Create dedicated verification methods in page object classes that return boolean values. Assertion statements in test scripts should call these methods. Method names should clearly indicate what is being verified.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Decompose Test Steps into Atomic Automation Actions
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Each test step must be broken down into granular intermediary steps that represent atomic automation actions: locate element, verify state, perform action, wait for response, confirm result.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test steps during automation script development
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Intermediary steps must be documented for complex test steps and implicit steps
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Follow the standard intermediary step pattern: (1) Locate/Identify element, (2) Verify element state (visible, enabled), (3) Perform action, (4) Wait for system response, (5) Confirm action result. Each intermediary step should be independently verifiable.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Implement Explicit Waits for UI State Changes
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All intermediary steps that trigger UI changes (navigation, popup display, screen transitions) must include explicit wait conditions for the resulting UI elements to become available and interactive.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all steps involving UI transitions, asynchronous operations, or dynamic content loading
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Scripts without proper wait conditions will fail reliability standards
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Use explicit waits with meaningful timeout values (default 10-30 seconds). Wait for specific conditions: element visibility, element clickability, text presence, element staleness. Avoid fixed sleep statements except for known animation durations.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Encapsulate UI Interactions in Page Object Methods
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All UI element interactions and verifications must be encapsulated in page object class methods. Test scripts should only call page object methods, never directly interact with UI elements.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all automation scripts across all test cases
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Direct element interaction in test scripts is prohibited
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Create page object classes for each application screen/component. Define methods for all interactions (click, input, select) and verifications (verify visibility, verify text, verify state). Use descriptive method names that reflect business actions.

page_object_structure.locators: Define all element locators as class variables
page_object_structure.action_methods: Methods that perform UI actions (click, type, select)
page_object_structure.verification_methods: Methods that return boolean indicating verification success

automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Before performing any action on a UI element, automation scripts must verify the element is in the correct state: visible, enabled, and interactable. This prevents flaky test failures.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all UI interaction steps
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Element state verification must precede all click, input, and selection actions
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Implement a standard verification sequence in page object action methods: (1) Verify element exists in DOM, (2) Verify element is visible, (3) Verify element is enabled, (4) Perform action, (5) Verify action completed. Use framework-specific element state checking methods.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Validate Popup Elements and Button Positioning
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: When validating popup windows or dialogs, automation scripts must verify: (1) Popup is displayed, (2) All expected buttons are present, (3) Button positioning matches specification (primary vs secondary), (4) Button text is correct, (5) Buttons are interactable.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test cases validating popup windows, dialogs, modals, or overlays
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Popup validation must be comprehensive and cover all specified elements
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Create dedicated popup validation methods that check all aspects: container visibility, title/header text, button presence and order, button text content, button states. For button positioning validation, verify CSS properties or layout order.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Create Reusable Setup and Navigation Methods
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Common implicit steps that appear across multiple test cases (app launch, navigation, login) must be extracted into reusable setup methods or fixtures to ensure consistency and reduce maintenance overhead.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to implicit steps that appear in 3 or more test cases
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: RECOMMENDED - Reusable methods improve maintainability and consistency
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Identify common implicit step sequences across test cases. Create base test classes or utility modules with reusable setup methods. Use test framework fixtures (pytest fixtures, unittest setUp) for test-level setup. Document reusable methods with clear parameters and expected outcomes.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Implement Graceful Failure and Diagnostic Logging
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Automation scripts must implement error handling for each intermediary step with diagnostic logging that captures: step name, failure reason, application state, screenshot, and relevant element properties.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all automation scripts
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Scripts must provide actionable failure diagnostics
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Wrap intermediary steps in try-except blocks with specific exception handling. On failure, log: timestamp, step description, exception type and message, current screen/page, element locator attempted, screenshot filename. Use logging levels appropriately (ERROR for failures, INFO for step completion, DEBUG for detailed actions).

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Use Boolean-Returning Verification Methods with Assert Statements
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: All verification methods in page objects must return boolean values (True for success, False for failure). Test scripts must use assert statements to evaluate these boolean returns, enabling clear pass/fail determination.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all verification and validation methods
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Verification methods must return boolean; test scripts must use assert statements
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Design verification methods to perform checks and return True if all conditions pass, False otherwise. In test scripts, use 'assert' keyword with verification method calls. Include optional assertion messages for clarity. Avoid verification methods that raise exceptions directly.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Externalize Test Data from Automation Scripts
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Test data (expected text, button labels, screen titles, validation values) must be externalized from automation scripts into configuration files, data files, or constants modules to support maintainability and localization.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test cases with validation data
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: RECOMMENDED - Externalized test data improves maintainability
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Create test data files (JSON, YAML, CSV) or constants modules containing expected values. Reference test data in verification methods using keys or identifiers. For the current test case, externalize expected button labels ('Yes, cancel', 'Go back') and popup titles.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Verify Test Preconditions Before Test Execution
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Automation scripts must verify all preconditions specified in test case custom_preconds field before executing test steps. If preconditions are not met, test should be skipped with appropriate reporting.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test cases with defined preconditions
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Precondition verification prevents invalid test execution
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Parse custom_preconds field from test case metadata. Implement precondition verification methods that check: printer availability, user login state, required data presence, system configuration. Execute precondition checks in test setup phase. Use test framework skip mechanisms if preconditions fail.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Confirm Current Screen Before Performing Actions
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Before executing actions on a screen, automation scripts must confirm the application is on the expected screen by verifying screen-specific elements (title, unique identifiers, key components).
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all navigation and action steps
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Screen context validation prevents actions on wrong screens
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: At the start of each action sequence on a new screen, verify screen identity by checking: screen title, unique element presence, URL/route (for web apps), or activity name (for mobile apps). Include screen context verification in intermediary steps for supporting actions.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: When validating buttons, verify comprehensive properties: presence, visibility, enabled state, text content, styling (primary/secondary designation), position/order, and click responsiveness.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test cases validating button elements, especially button positioning and hierarchy
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY for test cases specifically validating button properties; RECOMMENDED for general button interactions

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Set Validation Context in Supporting Steps
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Supporting steps that trigger validation scenarios must set explicit context for subsequent validation steps. This includes storing references to triggered elements, capturing initial states, or setting flags indicating validation readiness.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all supporting steps marked as 'Purpose of Test Case Validation'
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - Supporting steps must prepare context for validation steps
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: In supporting step implementation (e.g., clicking back button to trigger popup), after performing the action: (1) Wait for triggered element (popup) to appear, (2) Store reference to popup element for validation steps, (3) Set validation context flags, (4) Optionally capture initial state for comparison. Validation steps should reference this context.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Leverage Test Case Metadata for Automation Configuration
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Automation scripts must utilize test case metadata fields (priority_id, type_id, custom fields) to configure test execution behavior, reporting tags, and validation criteria.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all automated test cases
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: RECOMMENDED - Metadata utilization improves test organization and reporting
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Parse test case metadata at test initialization. Use priority_id for test execution ordering, type_id for categorization, custom_expected for validation criteria, custom_preconds for precondition setup. Tag test reports with test_case_id and metadata for traceability.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Ensure All Expected Outcomes Are Validated
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: Automation scripts must validate all expected outcomes specified in the test case custom_expected field. Each assertion should map to a specific expected outcome statement.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all test cases with defined expected outcomes
automation_scripts_rules.enforcement: MANDATORY - All expected outcomes must have corresponding assertions
automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Parse custom_expected field to identify all expected outcomes. Create verification methods for each outcome. For test case C48, expected outcome specifies button positions: create assertions for (1) 'Yes, cancel' as primary button, (2) 'Go back' as secondary button. Ensure both assertions are present in automation script.

automation_scripts_rules.rule_name: Document Automation Patterns for Reuse in Similar Test Cases
automation_scripts_rules.rule_description: For each automated test case, document the automation patterns, page object methods, and intermediary step sequences used. This documentation enables consistent automation of similar test cases in the future.
automation_scripts_rules.applicability: Apply to all automated test cases, especially those establishing new patterns

automation_scripts_rules.implementation_guidance: Create automation pattern documentation that includes: (1) Test case type and validation focus, (2) Page objects used, (3) Key verification methods created, (4) Intermediary step sequences, (5) Reusable components, (6) Similar test cases that can use same pattern.
